Expansion Slots

This document defines the two front-loading expansion slots, their electrical interface, connector pinout, address assignments, and card requirements. Return to the main page.

Revision 2.2 gives each slot five new contacts so a card can request motherboard DMA service on MC68450 channel 2 or channel 3. Cards still cannot arbitrate for the bus or drive the address lines. The five contacts come from former ground positions in rows a and c, so this is a connector revision and a revision 2.1 card is compatible only if it left those positions unconnected. Revision 2.1 added U_EXP_RW_BUF, which removes four direct loads from processor R_W; two buffer channels create EXP1_RW and EXP2_RW, and each branch drives one slot's control buffer and two data-transceiver DIR inputs. Each slot's I/O window sits in the protected I/O region and answers supervisor cycles only, while its 2 MiB memory window stays open to user-mode code and is not paged. Card drivers therefore run as BIOS code or as supervisor-mode extensions.

1. Purpose and Scope

The computer accepts two removable cards from the front of the enclosure. Guide rails carry each card to a DIN 41612 connector at the rear. Power must be off before a card is inserted or removed.

Each physical slot has one fixed 2 MiB memory window and one fixed 128 KiB I/O window. Moving a card between slots changes its addresses without jumpers or configuration storage. A card may use either or both windows, but it must not decode outside them.

The motherboard buffers every outgoing signal and gives each slot its own data transceivers. Cards cannot request the bus, become bus master, or drive the address and function-code lines. A card can ask the motherboard MC68450 to move bytes between the card and physical DRAM; section 10 gives that contract. An empty or nonresponding slot produces a bus error through the existing 51.1 microsecond minimum timeout.

2. Address Assignment

Fixed expansion-slot address windows
Slot Memory range Memory select I/O range I/O select
1 $400000-$5FFFFF EXP_MEM2_n $EC0000-$EDFFFF IO6_n
2 $600000-$7FFFFF EXP_MEM3_n $EE0000-$EFFFFF IO7_n

The connectors call these pins MEM_SEL_n and IO_SEL_n. Card schematics can use one connector symbol in either slot. A card that decodes fewer local address bits mirrors its registers or memory within its assigned window.

The two windows carry different privilege. IO6_n and IO7_n come from the top I/O decoder, which the motherboard closes to user-mode cycles, so a card's registers answer supervisor cycles only and a user-mode access to them takes a bus error. EXP_MEM2_n and EXP_MEM3_n carry no privilege test and no translation, so a card that presents plain memory can be handed to an application directly, at a fixed address rather than through its page table. Put control registers in the I/O window and bulk data in the memory window; see Supervisor Protection.

A card cannot bypass the protection, because no card drives the address bus. A card that could would see no FC2 test at all, which is one more reason the interface leaves /BR and /BGACK off the connector. Motherboard DMA service does not weaken this: the MC68450 drives the address itself, under a channel program that only the BIOS writes, and the BIOS validates every physical range before it starts.

EXP_MEM5_n and EXP_MEM6_n no longer select nothing. Memory-map revision 2.0 gives $A00000-$DFFFFF to the page-table aperture in Paging, so those two selects reach the page unit and the address space behind them is no longer available for a third and fourth expansion memory window. IO9_n selects the PI/T and IO10_n the page-unit control registers, so the only decode outputs still without a destination are IO11_n through IO14_n.

3. Mechanical Interface

Each card uses a 100 mm by 160 mm, 1.6 mm thick PCB with a 96-contact right-angle male DIN 41612 connector on its rear edge. A 3U front panel, approximately 128.4 mm high and 30.48 mm wide, gives each card a 6 HP bay. Both bays need about 61 mm of chassis width.

The 6 HP pitch permits a 20 mm component envelope on the component side and a 4 mm lead-and-solder envelope on the other side. Printed upper and lower guide channels support the card edges. Print the guides in PETG, ABS, or nylon rather than PLA.

Each front panel uses a printed pull handle and two cam ejectors on M3 pivots. The cams bear on reinforced chassis ledges, seat the connector evenly, and break it free before the user pulls the handle. Captive M3 thumbscrews at the top and bottom retain the seated card. The cams shall provide at least 3:1 mechanical advantage over their first 3 mm of travel.

Selected connector pair
Location Part Form
Card HARTING 09 03 196 2921 Type C, 96-contact, performance-level-1 male, right-angle through-hole
Motherboard HARTING 09 03 296 2824 Type C, 96-contact, performance-level-1 female, straight through-hole

The pair is specified for at least 500 mating cycles and up to 90 N insertion force. Use side-coding hardware so an expansion card cannot enter another DIN bay. Both expansion slots use the same key. The guides shall prevent one-row or one-position offset mating.

4. Architecture

address/control --+-- slot 1 HCT244 banks --> J_EXP1
                  +-- slot 2 HCT244 banks --> J_EXP2

CPU D15..D0 <--> slot 1 HCT245 pair <--> J_EXP1
             +--> slot 2 HCT245 pair <--> J_EXP2

J_EXP1 CARD_DTACK_n --+
                       +-- FAST AND --> EXP_DTACK_n --> completion tree
J_EXP2 CARD_DTACK_n --+

J_EXP1 EXP_IRQ_n -----+
                       +-- wired-OR --> level-3 interrupt
J_EXP2 EXP_IRQ_n -----+

J_EXP1 CARD_DMA_REQ_n / READY_n --> MC68450 REQ2 / PCL2
J_EXP2 CARD_DMA_REQ_n / READY_n --> MC68450 REQ3 / PCL3
ACK2_n, ACK3_n --> spare HCT244 channel --> CARD_DMA_ACK_n
ACKx_n + DTC_n / DONE_n --> U_EXP_DMA_OR --> per-slot DTC / DONE
ACKx_n + DTACK_n + CARD_DMA_READY_n --> F00, F08 --> PCL2 / PCL3

Separate drivers remove one card's connector and trace capacitance from the other card's signal path. The processor-side ports of the data transceivers share D15..D0, but fixed nonoverlapping selects enable only one slot. A card must still qualify every data driver and completion output with its connector select.

5. Signal Rules

Connector signal groups
Signals Direction at card Rule
A23..A1 Input Buffered address. Byte strobes replace external A0.
D15..D0 Bidirectional Drive requested lanes only during a selected read.
AS_n, UDS_n, LDS_n Input Active-low buffered bus strobes.
R_W Input High for read; low for write.
MEM_SEL_n, IO_SEL_n Input Active-low selects fixed by physical slot.
EXP_CLK_10 Input Buffered 10 MHz reference; frequency locked but not zero-skew to CPU clock.
PERIPH_RESET_n Input Active-low reset, including processor RESET instruction.
CARD_DTACK_n Open-collector output Pull low only for a selected, ready transfer.
EXP_IRQ_n Open-collector output Shared level-sensitive interrupt request.
CARD_DMA_REQ_n, CARD_DMA_READY_n Open-collector output Per-slot DMA request and ready. See section 10.
CARD_DMA_ACK_n, CARD_DMA_DTC_n, CARD_DMA_DONE_n Input Per-slot acknowledge, successful-transfer, and end-of-block signals. R_W describes memory while the acknowledge is low.

Bus logic uses +5 V TTL-compatible levels. Cards shall accept VIL <= 0.8 V and VIH >= 2.0 V and deliver VOL <= 0.4 V at the specified open-collector sink current. +12 V is power only and shall not touch a bus signal.

Row b is ground at every position. Six contacts carry +5 V, four carry +12 V, and 32 carry ground. Revision 2.2 took the five remaining ground contacts, a29, a32, c26, c29, and c32, for the DMA handshake in section 10, so row b is now the only return path. Parallel every contact assigned to the same rail on both boards and tie every row-b contact to the ground plane.

7. Address and Control Buffers

Each slot uses four SN74HCT244N packages. Three carry A23..A1; the fourth carries the strobes, direction, selects, clock, and reset. Both output-enable pins on every package are grounded. No card pin connects to a processor output or an unbuffered motherboard select.

Per-slot HCT244 allocation
Package Channels Signals
Address low 1 through 8 A1..A8
Address middle 1 through 8 A9..A16
Address high 1 through 7 A17..A23
Address high 8 ACK2_n or ACK3_n, producing CARD_DMA_ACK_n
Control 1 through 8 AS_n, EXPx_RW, UDS_n, LDS_n, memory select, I/O select, EXP_CLK_ROOT, PERIPH_RESET_n

Put a 33 ohm series resistor between every HCT244 output and its connector contact, and between each U_EXP_DMA_OR output and its contact. These 34 resistors per slot provide source damping and limit current during accidental contention.

8. Data Bus

Two SN74HCT245N packages serve each slot. A ports face the card; B ports face the motherboard. During CPU PIO, DIR follows EXPx_RW. During DMA, R/W describes the memory access, so invert it for the lower-byte transceiver. Keep the connector's EXPx_RW unchanged. The upper-byte transceiver stays disabled during DMA; the DMAC's HIBYTE bridge handles even-address memory bytes. 

EXP1_CYCLE_n = EXP_MEM2_n AND IO6_n
EXP2_CYCLE_n = EXP_MEM3_n AND IO7_n
DS_INACTIVE  = UDS_n AND LDS_n
CYCLE_END    = AS_n OR DS_INACTIVE
OWN_ACTIVE   = NOT OWN_n
EXP1_DMA_n   = ACK2_n OR OWN_n OR CYCLE_END
EXP2_DMA_n   = ACK3_n OR OWN_n OR CYCLE_END
EXPx_LOW_OE_n  = EXPx_CYCLE_n AND EXPx_DMA_n
EXPx_HIGH_OE_n = EXPx_CYCLE_n
EXPx_LOW_DIR   = EXPx_RW XOR OWN_ACTIVE
EXPx_HIGH_DIR  = EXPx_RW

CPU read:      DIR=1, card A --> motherboard B
CPU write:     DIR=0, motherboard B --> card A
DMA R/W=0:     DIR=1, card A --> memory (device-to-memory)
DMA R/W=1:     DIR=0, memory --> card A (memory-to-device)

Keep U_EXP_GLUE gates 1 and 2 for the PIO cycle terms. Add U_EXP_DMA_EN (SN74F08N): gate 1 computes DS_INACTIVE and gates 2 and 3 compute the slot-1 and slot-2 low enables. Add U_EXP_DMA_MASK_A and U_EXP_DMA_MASK_B (SN74F32N): A gates 1-4 compute CYCLE_END, ACK2_n OR OWN_n, ACK3_n OR OWN_n, and EXP1_DMA_n; B gate 1 computes EXP2_DMA_n. Add U_EXP_DMA_DIR (SN74F86N), gates 1 and 2, for the two lower-byte DIR signals. These 14-pin gate packages use A/B/Y pins 1/2/3, 4/5/6, 9/10/8, and 12/13/11; pin 7 is ground and pin 14 is +5 V. Ground unused inputs, leave unused outputs open, and add a 100 nF bypass capacitor at each package.

U_EXP_RW_BUF remains an SN74HCT244N with two R_W inputs. Each output drives its connector R/W contact, upper-byte DIR, and one XOR input. OWN settles before DMA cycles. Raw AS and byte-strobe qualification keep the DMA data path disabled during address/direction setup and descriptor fetches without ACK. Check DIR setup before /OE at the HCT245 pins using the MC68450 strobe timing and the added FAST gate delays. Include the two new XOR loads on OWN_ACTIVE in the DMA ownership fanout budget. CPU PIO still passes all 16 bits; cards qualify their byte lanes. Add these four FAST packages and their bypass capacitors to the motherboard interface supply budget, outside the card rail allowance.

Card byte-lane behavior
UDS_n LDS_n Requested lane Action
0 1 D15..D8 Upper-byte device may respond.
1 0 D7..D0 Lower-byte device may respond.
0 0 Both A 16-bit device uses both. An 8-bit device uses its own lane only.
1 1 None Do not drive data or completion.

Lower-lane 8-bit cards connect to D7..D0, respond to LDS_n, and place canonical registers at odd addresses. Upper-lane cards use D15..D8, UDS_n, and even addresses.

9. Cycle Completion

Each connector has a separate CARD_DTACK_n net and a motherboard 1 kohm, 5 percent pull-up. Cards use an open-collector or open-drain output and never drive high. Gate 3 of U_EXP_GLUE combines the inputs: 

EXP_DTACK_n = EXP1_CARD_DTACK_n AND EXP2_CARD_DTACK_n

The push-pull result enters U_DTACK_B gate 1 in the shared completion tree. A card may assert completion only while its select and a supported byte strobe are active. For reads, requested data must already be valid. For writes, the card must have accepted or be ready to accept the data.

Release completion as soon as the select or all supported strobes negate. A card that cannot finish within 50 microseconds leaves the line high and lets the motherboard timeout produce a bus error. Every completion output shall sink at least 8 mA at 0.4 V. One SN74LS07N channel meets this rule.

10. DMA Service

A card cannot arbitrate for the bus, drive the address or function-code lines, or become a master. Revision 2.2 gives it a different thing: it can ask the motherboard MC68450 to move a byte between the card and physical DRAM. Slot 1 uses channel 2 and slot 2 uses channel 3. The controller drives the address, the strobes, and the acknowledge; the card only raises a request and accepts or supplies one byte per acknowledge.

Per-slot DMA contacts added in revision 2.2
Contact Signal Direction at card Rule
c26 CARD_DMA_REQ_n Open-collector output Pull low to request one transfer and hold it low until CARD_DMA_ACK_n asserts. A 2.2 kohm motherboard pull-up holds it inactive. Sink at least 4 mA at 0.4 V.
a29 CARD_DMA_ACK_n Input Active-low acknowledge from the channel assigned to this slot. It selects the card's DMA port; no address is valid during it.
c29 CARD_DMA_READY_n Open-collector output Pull low when the card has data on the bus, or can accept it. A 2.2 kohm motherboard pull-up holds it inactive.
a32 CARD_DMA_DTC_n Input Active-low pulse marking a successful transfer. This, not the acknowledge, is what advances a card FIFO or pointer.
c32 CARD_DMA_DONE_n Input Active-low during the last transfer of the current descriptor. Combined with CARD_DMA_DTC_n it marks the end of a block. 
CARD_DMA_REQ_n   -> MC68450 REQ2 or REQ3
CARD_DMA_READY_n -> MC68450 PCL2 or PCL3
CARD_DMA_ACK_n   = ACK2_n or ACK3_n
CARD_DMA_DTC_n   = ACKx_n OR DTC_n
CARD_DMA_DONE_n  = ACKx_n OR DONE_n

Qualifying the two motherboard outputs with the slot's own acknowledge keeps another channel's completion off this connector. The shared open-drain DONE_n net and the three-stated DTC_n net never reach a card directly.

Transfer Contract

Each transfer moves one byte on D7..D0. An even memory address asserts UDS_n and the motherboard HIBYTE transceiver bridges the lanes; an odd address asserts LDS_n. The card stays on the lower lane in both cases and shall not decode the strobes to choose a lane of its own. A 16-bit card must still present its DMA port as eight bits, because single-address operand size has to equal the device port size.

During the acknowledge, R_W describes memory rather than the card. R_W low means the controller is writing memory, so the card drives D7..D0. R_W high means the controller is reading memory, so the card accepts D7..D0. This inverts the reading a card uses for its ordinary selected cycles, and a card that reuses one direction term for both will drive against the bus.

  1. The card pulls CARD_DMA_REQ_n low and holds it until the acknowledge asserts. Releasing early can lose the transfer.
  2. The motherboard asserts CARD_DMA_ACK_n. The card then drives or prepares to accept one byte.
  3. The card pulls CARD_DMA_READY_n low within 32 microseconds of the acknowledge. On a card-to-memory transfer it shall not assert ready before its data is valid on the bus. The motherboard bus timeout remains the outer limit, and a card that never answers takes a bus error.
  4. CARD_DMA_DTC_n pulses once the cycle has completed successfully. The card advances its FIFO or pointer on this pulse only. An acknowledge without a following CARD_DMA_DTC_n means the cycle faulted and the byte did not move.
  5. CARD_DMA_DONE_n accompanies the last transfer of the descriptor. A card that needs an end-of-block signal shall qualify it with CARD_DMA_DTC_n.
  6. The card releases CARD_DMA_READY_n after the acknowledge negates, and may raise a new request.

Channels 2 and 3 use the acknowledge-and-ready protocol, so the MC68450 also samples the ready input during its descriptor fetches, when no acknowledge is asserted. Motherboard logic supplies that ready from DTACK_n whenever the slot's acknowledge is inactive, exactly as manual Figure 4-12 requires. A card sees nothing of those cycles and shall not drive the bus while its acknowledge is high.

Limits

Both expansion channels share one priority level below the floppy, so the controller alternates between them in round robin. The floppy keeps the highest priority because its FIFO has a hard service deadline. An expansion card therefore cannot assume a bounded request-to-acknowledge interval better than the budget in DMA Controller, and the 32 microsecond ready limit above is what keeps one card out of another device's deadline.

The BIOS owns every channel program. A card driver asks for a transfer through a BIOS call gate, which validates the physical range, direction, and count, pins the buffer, and records the owning process. A card cannot reach a page-table entry, an I/O register, or another process's memory: the controller drives supervisor data function codes at addresses the BIOS has already checked, and three hardware interlocks stop a DMA cycle leaving main memory even when that check is wrong.

The BIOS may also borrow either channel for a memory copy, which reprograms it for dual-address transfers between two DRAM ranges. A slot's channel is available for that only while the slot's driver holds no claim on it, so the driver takes the slot's DMA lock whenever the card may raise a request and releases it when the card is quiescent. A card that requests service on a borrowed channel gets nothing back and no error, and would starve its own FIFO. The lock is part of the driver contract.

The five contacts come from the ground positions in rows a and c, so a revision 2.2 motherboard leaves 32 ground contacts, all in row b, instead of 37. Every card and the motherboard shall tie each row-b contact to its ground plane with a short via so the power contacts at positions 27 through 31 keep a low-impedance return.

A revision 2.1 card still works in a revision 2.2 slot only if it leaves those five contacts unconnected. A card that bonded them to its ground plane will short two motherboard outputs and load two pull-ups, so check the card's connector assignment before fitting it.

Motherboard Glue

U_EXP_DMA_OR, an SN74F32N, qualifies both broadcast completion signals with each slot's own acknowledge. All four gates are used.

U_EXP_DMA_OR SN74F32N connections
Gate Inputs Output
1: pins 1, 2 to 3 ACK2_n, DTC_n Slot 1 CARD_DMA_DTC_n
2: pins 4, 5 to 6 ACK2_n, DONE_n Slot 1 CARD_DMA_DONE_n
3: pins 9, 10 to 8 ACK3_n, DTC_n Slot 2 CARD_DMA_DTC_n
4: pins 12, 13 to 11 ACK3_n, DONE_n Slot 2 CARD_DMA_DONE_n
Power Pin 14 to +5 V Pin 7 to ground

The acknowledge itself reaches the connector through the spare eighth channel of each slot's address-high HCT244, which revision 2.1 left grounded. Every outgoing card signal therefore still comes from a buffer rather than from a shared motherboard net, and each of the three new outputs takes a 33 ohm series resistor like the rest.

CARD_DMA_REQ_n runs from the connector straight to the MC68450 REQ2 or REQ3 pin, with a 2.2 kohm motherboard pull-up at the controller end. CARD_DMA_READY_n reaches PCL2 or PCL3 through the ready circuit below, and carries the same pull-up at the connector. Both values come from the release-time and sink-current work in DMA Controller; cards fit no pull-up of their own.

Channels 2 and 3 use array chaining, and manual Figure 4-12 requires the ready input to be asserted during the controller's own chain-table accesses, when no acknowledge is active. Two gate packages build the circuit that figure specifies. 

DTACK_ACT     = NOT DTACK_n
EXPx_PCL_TERM = NOT (ACKx_n AND DTACK_ACT)
PCLx_n        = EXPx_CARD_READY_n AND EXPx_PCL_TERM
U_EXP_DMA_NAND SN74F00N and U_EXP_DMA_AND SN74F08N connections
Gate Inputs Output
NAND 1: pins 1, 2 to 3 Both to DTACK_n DTACK_ACT
NAND 2: pins 4, 5 to 6 ACK2_n, DTACK_ACT EXP1_PCL_TERM
NAND 3: pins 9, 10 to 8 ACK3_n, DTACK_ACT EXP2_PCL_TERM
NAND 4: pins 12, 13 to 11 Ground both Open
AND 1: pins 1, 2 to 3 EXP1_CARD_READY_n, EXP1_PCL_TERM PCL2_n
AND 2: pins 4, 5 to 6 EXP2_CARD_READY_n, EXP2_PCL_TERM PCL3_n
AND 3 and 4 Ground pins 9, 10, 12, and 13 Pins 8 and 11 open
Power Pin 14 of each to +5 V Pin 7 of each to ground

While the slot's acknowledge is low, PCL follows the card alone. While it is high, PCL follows motherboard DTACK_n, which covers the chain-table fetches. The manual notes that the same circuit asserts ready during cycles the channel is not running and that the controller ignores its ready input then; processor cycles reach the gate and do the same. That sets the PCL transition bit in CSR, which firmware ignores on a channel programmed for ready and clears with the rest of the register. The IDE channel gates its equivalent path with BGACK_n because a spare gate was free there. The slots use Motorola's plain circuit instead of spending another package on a status bit nobody reads.

11. Interrupts

Both connectors share EXP_IRQ_n. The existing 4.7 kohm motherboard pull-up holds it high; either card can pull it low. It enters the priority encoder at level 3 and receives autovector 27, whose exception-vector address is $00006C.

A card keeps its request low until its driver clears every enabled cause. The level-3 handler polls both installed drivers and repeats while the line remains low. Interrupt assertion gives no permission to drive data or completion; the motherboard terminates the acknowledge with /AVEC.

12. Clock and Reset

Gate 1 of U_EXP_CLK_PHASE, an SN74F04N, reads the complementary 10 MHz divider output at U_CPU_CLK pin 8. It produces EXP_CLK_ROOT, a nominally in-phase copy of CPU_CLK_10. The per-slot control HCT244s drive separate connector clocks from that root.

Pin 8 continues to drive pin 12 for toggle feedback. Include the F04 input in the divider feedback waveform check. Cards may use the connector clock for state machines and baud-rate division, but shall not assume specified edge skew from the CPU clock. A card-side buffer is required for more than two clock loads.

PERIPH_RESET_n asserts for power-on reset, manual reset, and the CPU RESET instruction. A card with active-high reset inverts it locally. A device without reset shall keep bus outputs disabled until its software initialization is complete.

13. Power Distribution

Each slot has separate protection. An RXEF250 radial resettable fuse feeds +5 V, and an RXEF110 feeds +12 V. Cards may draw no more than 1.0 A continuously from +5 V and 0.4 A from +12 V. Reduce those limits if measured fuse or enclosure temperature requires it.

Per-slot power network
Rail Protection Motherboard capacitance Card limit
+5 V RXEF250, 2.50 A hold at 20 C and 1.35 A at 70 C 100 uF / 10 V plus 100 nF after fuse 1.0 A
+12 V RXEF110, 1.10 A hold at 20 C and 0.59 A at 70 C 47 uF / 25 V plus 100 nF after fuse 0.4 A

The system supply shall cover the motherboard plus 2.0 A on +5 V and 0.8 A on +12 V with both slots full. A card shall not feed current back into either rail. Put at least 47 uF on card +5 V, 10 uF on card +12 V, and 100 nF at every IC. Do not exceed 1000 uF per card rail without checking supply startup and fuse behavior again.

The connector has no make-first sequence. Label the front panel POWER OFF BEFORE REMOVING CARD. Software shutdown does not make live insertion or removal safe.

14. Card Requirements

Mandatory card-interface limits
Item Requirement
IC age Every IC design was commercially available by December 31, 1993. Later datasheet revisions are allowed.
Packages ICs are through-hole. Passives may be surface-mount.
Address/control No more than 20 pF and two HCT-equivalent inputs per pin. Buffer more fanout locally.
Data No more than 20 pF per pin while unselected. Three-state every inactive read driver.
Completion No more than 50 pF; open-collector sink of at least 8 mA at 0.4 V.
Interrupt Open collector; no card pull-up; no more than 50 pF.
Bus hold No pull resistor, bus-hold cell, or terminator on data, selects, or strobes.
Bus mastering Never drive address, select, strobe, direction, clock, or reset pins.
DMA handshake Open collector on request and ready, no card pull-up, sink at least 4 mA at 0.4 V, no more than 50 pF. No more than two HCT-equivalent inputs on each acknowledge, DTC, and DONE contact.
DMA port Eight bits on D7..D0. Reverse the R_W interpretation while the acknowledge is low, and advance the port only on CARD_DMA_DTC_n.
Unused DMA contacts A card that does not use DMA leaves a29, a32, c26, c29, and c32 unconnected. It shall not tie them to ground.
External power Do not back-power either card rail from a front-panel connector.

Cards may use TTL, LS, F, HC, HCT, ACT, or another period-correct 5 V family when the complete interface meets these limits. Plain HC inputs are not suitable for motherboard signals guaranteed high at only 2.0 V. HCT inputs are the default.

Protect external ports against cable discharge and out-of-range voltage at the front panel. Do not return cable-shield current through a bus ground contact when the enclosure provides chassis ground.

15. Software Contract

The bus has no enumeration register. System configuration identifies the card and driver in each physical slot. Probing an empty slot causes a bus error, so discovery code needs a temporary bus-error handler or saved configuration. Probing runs in the BIOS, which is the only code that can reach the I/O windows.

Driver-visible slot bases
Slot Memory Lower-byte I/O Upper-byte I/O
1 $400000 $EC0001 $EC0000
2 $600000 $EE0001 $EE0000

Drivers use byte operations for 8-bit registers unless a card defines the unused word byte. The shared level-3 handler polls both card drivers, clears every reported cause, and polls again if EXP_IRQ_n stays low. Every address in the two I/O columns is supervisor only, so a driver runs inside the BIOS and exposes its card to applications through BIOS services. The memory column needs no privilege, so a driver may hand a memory window to an application once it has configured the card.

16. Example 8-Bit Register Card

This lower-byte read/write latch tests either slot. It responds throughout the slot's I/O window, so its canonical register is $EC0001 in slot 1 or $EE0001 in slot 2. It ignores MEM_SEL_n and does not request interrupts. 

D7..D0 --> HCT574 register --> HCT244 read driver --> D7..D0

IO_SEL_n + LDS_n + R_W  --> write strobe --> HCT574 CLK
IO_SEL_n + LDS_n + /R_W --> read enable  --> HCT244 OE_n
IO_SEL_n + LDS_n -------> three-stage HCT74 delay
                                  |
                                  +--> HCT04 --> LS07 --> CARD_DTACK_n

Logic equations

NOT_R_W      = NOT R_W
EX_WRITE_n   = IO_SEL_n OR LDS_n OR R_W
EX_READ_n    = IO_SEL_n OR LDS_n OR NOT_R_W
EX_ACCESS_n  = IO_SEL_n OR LDS_n
EX_ACCESS    = NOT EX_ACCESS_n
EX_ACK_CLR_n = EX_ACCESS AND PERIPH_RESET_n

stage 1 D = 1; stage 2 D = stage 1 Q; stage 3 D = stage 2 Q
all stage clocks = EXP_CLK_10; all CLR_n inputs = EX_ACK_CLR_n
all PRE_n inputs = 1
CARD_DTACK_n = open-collector copy of stage 3 /Q

U_EX_REG clocks on the rising edge of EX_WRITE_n when the selected write ends. Its data has been stable throughout the write strobe. U_EX_READ drives only while the I/O select, lower strobe, and read direction are active.

Three flip-flops in U_EX_ACK_A and U_EX_ACK_B, both SN74HCT74N packages, shift a one down the chain. Their asynchronous clear stays low while unselected or reset. The third stage allows at least two full 10 MHz periods for read data before its complementary output pulls completion low. Select release clears the chain and releases completion without waiting for a clock.

Example-card parts
Reference Part Function
U_EX_REG SN74HCT574N Eight-bit write register
U_EX_READ SN74HCT244N Lower-byte read driver
U_EX_OR SN74HCT32N Access qualification
U_EX_INV SN74HCT04N Direction and access inversions
U_EX_AND SN74HCT08N Acknowledgement clear
U_EX_ACK_A, U_EX_ACK_B 2 x SN74HCT74N Three-clock response delay
U_EX_OC SN74LS07N Open-collector completion

Ground unused logic inputs and leave their outputs open. Fit 100 nF at every IC and 47 uF across card +5 V and ground. The example does not use +12 V.

Example-card package connections

On U_EX_OR, pins 1 and 2 receive IO_SEL_n and LDS_n; pin 3 is EX_ACCESS_n. Pins 4 and 5 receive EX_ACCESS_n and R_W; pin 6 is EX_WRITE_n. Pins 9 and 10 receive EX_ACCESS_n and NOT_R_W; pin 8 is EX_READ_n. Ground pins 12 and 13 and leave pin 11 open.

U_EX_INV uses pins 1 to 2 for R_W to NOT_R_W and pins 3 to 4 for EX_ACCESS_n to EX_ACCESS. U_EX_AND uses pins 1 and 2 for EX_ACCESS and PERIPH_RESET_n; pin 3 is EX_ACK_CLR_n. Ground every remaining input on both packages.

U_EX_REG pin 1 is grounded, pin 11 receives EX_WRITE_n, pins 19 through 12 receive connector D0..D7, and pins 2 through 9 produce REG0..REG7. Connect those register outputs to U_EX_READ in the common HCT244 channel order from section 16. Its two output-enable pins receive EX_READ_n, and its outputs drive connector D0..D7.

18. Timing and Electrical Checks

Outgoing and data paths

At 4.5 V and 50 pF, the SN74HCT244 has 42 ns maximum propagation delay over the chosen temperature range. The card's 20 pF limit leaves 30 pF for connector, resistor, trace, socket, and probe. Under the same conditions, the commercial SN74HCT245 has 28 ns maximum data delay and 58 ns maximum enable time. A card includes that delay and places read data before it asserts completion.

Completion assertion

Assertion is a falling edge at every node, so each stage uses its high-to-low maximum. 

U_EXP_GLUE F08, tPHL                 6.3 ns
two F21 completion levels, tPHL     11.0 ns
F32 timeout mask, tPHL               6.3 ns
component subtotal                  23.6 ns

This excludes card, connector, and trace delay. A synchronous card asserts after its data is stable and holds both through the processor's terminating edge.

Completion release

With 50 pF card load, another 50 pF for the connector path and probe, a 1.05 kohm maximum pull-up, and a 4.75 V rail, an ideal RC node reaches the FAST 2.0 V threshold in 57.4 ns: 

t = -1050 ohms * 100 pF * ln(1 - 2.0 / 4.75) = 57.4 ns

Release is a rising edge at every node, so each stage uses its low-to-high maximum: 6.6 ns through the F08, 10.6 ns through two F21 levels, and 6.6 ns through the F32. The 81.2 ns total leaves 28.8 ns for board delay against the CPU's 110 ns completion-release limit. If measurement misses the limit, reduce capacitance or lower the pull-up after checking card sink current. 

RC to the 2.0 V FAST threshold      57.4 ns
U_EXP_GLUE F08, tPLH                 6.6 ns
two F21 completion levels, tPLH     10.6 ns
F32 timeout mask, tPLH               6.6 ns
------------------------------------------------
component total                     81.2 ns
MC68EC000 limit                    110.0 ns
board allowance                     28.8 ns

DC levels

Two slot-buffer inputs add at most 2 uA DC load to each CPU signal. At 4.5 V, an HCT244 guarantees at least 3.84 V while sourcing 6 mA and no more than 0.33 V while sinking 6 mA. Margins to the card's 2.0 V and 0.8 V thresholds are 1.84 V high and 0.47 V low before interconnect drop.

Every listed IC design predates 1994. HCT logic was established in the 1980s; the HCT245 and HCT574 documents date their designs to 1984, HCT32 to 1988, and LS07 to no later than 1990. The FAST family appears in the 1980 Fairchild data book. Later datasheet revisions do not change the period rule.

20. Board Layout

  • Place each slot's buffers behind its connector and every 33 ohm resistor at its driver.
  • Join row-b contacts to a ground plane with short vias; use wide pours for power and ground.
  • Record routed completion capacitance and delay, then repeat the 110 ns release check with a probe.
  • Model guides, ejectors, reaction ledges, captive fasteners, and connector alignment before fixing motherboard holes.

21. Assembled-System Acceptance

Expansion-interface acceptance checks
Check Required result
Insertion Cards seat evenly and cannot mate one row or position off.
Retention Front controls and cables do not move a retained card.
Power Maximum card load stays in every device's supply range; a slot short trips its own fuse.
Address isolation Each slot responds only in its assigned windows; reserved ranges bus-error.
Byte lanes Upper, lower, and word tests show no drive on unrequested lanes.
Empty slot Access ends in a timeout bus error without contention.
Completion Read data precedes assertion; release reaches CPU /DTACK high within 110 ns.
Clock and reset Both connectors receive a clean 10 MHz clock and every defined reset pulse.
Interrupt Either or both cards request level 3; the line releases after every cause clears.
Cross-slot isolation One card causes no false select, data drive, completion, or interrupt in the other.
DMA handshake A test card's request reaches the assigned channel, the acknowledge appears only at that slot, and the qualified DTC and DONE pulses appear only during that slot's acknowledge.
Descriptor ready With the acknowledge inactive, PCL2 and PCL3 follow motherboard DTACK_n, and a chained transfer completes its chain-table fetches without stalling.
DMA data Both directions move the expected bytes at even and odd memory addresses, and the card drives nothing while its acknowledge is high.
DMA fault An injected bus error suppresses CARD_DMA_DTC_n, the card's pointer does not advance, and the BIOS terminates the recorded owner.
Contact migration A revision 2.1 card with the five former ground contacts unconnected runs without change; a card that grounds them is detected before power-on.
